# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — build capability from empty seed on the measured sibling champion + narrow its one regression (date component → int)
- Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
  - prompt.md (new, ~2500 words) + task_template.md (new): copied from sibling run `reused_seed_run` accepted cand_0001 (same seed/val/model; val 0.95). Levers: grading CONTRACT (values not formulas; typed values; preserve originals) → clusters A/B/C; HOW TO WORK inspect→calibrate→write→reopen→verify→stop → D/E; prompt §2 "workbook tells you the answer shape" conditional rules → F; §4 preserve-everything / conditional openpyxl → C/G.
  - task_template.md CONTRACT item 2: appended one sentence — the `datetime` rule covers an answer that IS a date; a number taken OUT of a date ("number of the day", "which month", "the year") is a plain int → cluster H (31628).
- Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe: base expected ≈ sibling's 0.95 (fixed 37378, 46897, 53383, 55049, 6698, 7902, 8942, 37456, 53647, 54144, 56563, 48527, 50768, 39046, 227-40, 267-18, 55979, 59196, 43436, 9569, 51-12; broke 31628). The CONTRACT narrowing should restore 31628 (base trace cites "CONTRACT requires dates as datetime objects"); it only triggers on date-component wording, not on date-valued answers (12864, 416-15, 9726, 59595, 2768).
- Building on prior RESULTS: sibling cand_0002–0005 (rejected) all fixed 31628 with this narrowing but broke 43436/51-12 (mandatory ANSWER TYPE step), 395-36/48527/9569 (pruning, openpyxl default), 227-40/43436/9569 (max_row append filter + §1(b) bullet + tie-break). I shipped ONLY the one-sentence narrowing, none of those.
- Refuted hypotheses (sibling run): universal mandatory pre-write step; pruning the prompt; making openpyxl the default writer.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: 80-42 (consolidate into a sheet already holding rows; appends after the full extent → coverage mismatch). The sibling's max_row/data-extent filter fixed it only inside a bundle that broke others.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration).
- Focus next iteration: if accepted, try the 80-42 append-position fix ALONE (one bounded sentence in §4), and re-check whichever tasks flip with the per-task variance in mind (227-40, 43436, 9569, 51-12 are the volatile ones).

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.974 Δ=+0.524 · fixed={267-18, 37378, 37456, 39046, 46897, 48527, 50768, 51-12, 53383, 53647, 54144, 55049, 55979, 56563, 59196, 6698, 7902, 80-42, 8942, 9569} · broke={45635} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).
<!-- cand_0001: ACCEPTED val=0.974 Δ=+0.524 -->

## Iteration cand_0002 — fix column-letter off-by-one (43436) with an address-keyed inspection printout + verify item
- Changes I made:
  - task_template.md Phase 1 recipe: neighbour rows now print as `[(coordinate, value)]` for non-empty cells (≤30 cols), plus one sentence: take each column letter you write from this printout, by the header that names the quantity, never by counting preview headers. (cluster I: column mis-mapping)
  - prompt.md §3: new bullet explaining why counting headers slips (multi-word headers, `Unnamed: k`, positional lists hide letters) and that one shifted column shifts all later ones. (cluster I, knowledge)
  - task_template.md Phase 3 checklist: new item — each graded column's header names what you wrote; a column you believed "already filled" whose `was:` is `None` means the letters are shifted, so re-map. (cluster I, verify step)
- Expected effect + safety: 43436's trace computed the right snapshot counts, but it mapped "Open as of today" to I instead of H. So it wrote May/Jun into J/K, left I empty and skipped Jul. That accounts exactly for the feedback (6 shifted cells, 5 empty). With letters printed beside the headers, the mapping is read rather than counted. Safe: only 3/38 traces copied the old row loop (31628 and 560-12 pass), and they would now see the same values with addresses added. The §3 bullet and the checklist item fire only when the agent derives column letters or sees that contradiction. No decision rule, §2 semantics or calibration text was changed.
- Building on prior RESULTS: cand_0001 accepted (fixed 43436 on the sibling base via the §2 snapshot rule + Phase 1b). Its current failure is a different cause (column mapping), so the snapshot rule is kept as is. I did NOT re-try the sibling's refuted edits: mandatory ANSWER TYPE step, pruning, openpyxl-as-default, max_row append filter bundle.
- Refuted hypotheses: none new (no RESULT since cand_0001).
- Not yet cracked: none failing besides 43436. 227-40/45635 are ENV (sandbox `/execute` HTTP 500, trace=None, 0 agent turns). A human must check the sandbox service.
- Plateau signal: val 0.974 with 1 capability failure left; remaining gain is mostly noise-bound. If rejected as within noise, the next iteration should not keep tuning 43436. Instead it should re-measure, or work on test-split generalisation, using the same small and bounded edits.
- Focus next iteration: protect the 37 passers; consider only failures that newly appear in the traces.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.925 Δ=-0.049 · fixed={227-40, 43436} · broke={267-18, 37456} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them). — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.
